messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Synthetic check failure - canary-probe /api/health in eu-west-1. 95% failures in last 2m. PagerDuty incident PD-8421 created.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Triggered PD-8421 -> canary-failure-eu-west-1. Escalation policy: oncall-sre.

jordan (oncall): ack'd. I'm on it, pulling logs and the canary dashboard. Anyone else seeing this from other regions?

maya (SRE): seeing similar small spike in us-west-2 but only ~5% failures. eu-west looks bad. Sharing quick query: `sum(rate(canary_failed[1m])) by (region)` shows eu-west ~ 38/min.

lee (prod-eng): reported from monitoring: backend-frontend timeouts to model-proxy instance pool in eu-west-1. 502/504s. No deploys in last 2 hours.

jordan (oncall): running `kubectl get pods -n canary-metrics -o wide` -> a few probe-agents CrashLoopBackOff on nodes ip-10-...

arjun (SRE): copying probe logs: ```2025-10-29T12:01:07Z probe: dial tcp 10.2.5.17:8080: connect: connection refused
2025-10-29T12:01:08Z probe: health check failed: EOF```

maya (SRE): possible network flapping between probe agents and model-proxy. Tracing from vpc-nat shows dropped connections to nodes on the same AZ. Opening ticket with infra? @lee can you confirm any node maintenance?

lee (prod-eng): Nothing scheduled. I'm seeing increased retransmits on that AZ's host interfaces. Paging infra/network oncall.

incident-bot: Update: PD-8421 -> acknowledged by jordan. Next escalation in 10m if no progress.

jordan (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) disable synthetic canary in eu-west to stop noise and reduce paging, 2) revert canary agent rollout (if any), 3) restart probe agents on affected nodes, 4) route real traffic unaffected — hold fallback rules. I'll start step 1 now.

maya (SRE): agreed. Do NOT touch model-proxy pools until we confirm; probes using different port. I'll coordinate with infra.

jordan (oncall): `./runbook canary-failure` -> following checklist. Executing: `curl -X POST https://console.internal/api/canaries/eu-west-1/disable` -> 200 OK. Stopping alert noise.

lee (prod-eng): infra oncall (Sam) responding: "saw NIC errors on i-0a3.., rolling a fix to the host level kernel pathing, will cordon and migrate affected instances." Sam asked to drain affected nodes slowly.

arjun (SRE): restarting probe agents on drained nodes: `kubectl rollout restart ds/canary-probe -n canary-metrics --selector=zone=eu-west-1a` -> pods coming back healthy.

maya (SRE): after probe restart, failure rate dropped to ~1% in eu-west. Good sign. Monitoring p95 latency for real traffic — stable.

jordan (oncall): PD-8421: adding note: "disabled canary in eu-west, infra applied host-level fix, restarted probe agents; canary failures decreased; no customer error reports yet."

lee (prod-eng): customer impact assessment: no increase in errors from production APIs; some internal dashboards experienced transient alerting but no user-facing 5xx spike. Marking impact: "no client-facing impact, internal monitoring noise".

maya (SRE): will keep canary disabled for 30m after infra confirms nodes healthy, then re-enable with reduced concurrency. Need a follow-up postmortem to track runbook gaps around host-level errors.

jordan (oncall): handing off to maya for the 23:00-23:30 watch window. I'll annotate the incident and drop into #postmortems. @maya please take ownership for follow-up.

maya (SRE): taking over. I'll collect metrics, annotate the runbook, and coordinate with infra for a permanent fix. Opening postmortem ticket: PM-5893.

incident-bot: PD-8421 -> resolved (manual resolution). Resolution note: canary disabled, infra fixed hosts, probes restarted.

arjun (SRE): quick action items: 1) add host NIC health check to canary-sensor, 2) add runbook step to confirm node kernel patch status before probe restarts, 3) adjust canary retry/backoff to avoid noisy pages.

jordan (oncall): thanks team. If anyone sees regression after re-enable, ping me direct. Closing thread after postmortem posted. :thumbsup:
